facts.fact: ANIP's director general states that in the six months of the pilot a little over 17,000 births were declared and more than 13,000 of them registered in the ten pilot one-stop desks, a rate above 76% (76.56%) against a national rate of about 22% in 2025.

ANIP's director general states that the pilot phase ran in ten health facilities and ended in February 2026, and that the consolidation phase that followed is running in the same ten facilities, with generalisation three to four months behind the initial calendar.

ANIP's director general states that at the one-stop desk declaration and registration are done in one process at the maternity before discharge, using digital tools, and that in the new phase health workers use new internet-connected terminals for declarations; paper declaration forms remained in use during the pilot, when stock-outs and duplicate form numbers were reported.

ANIP runs the one-stop birth registration desk with its own teams and the Ministry of Health's health workers, and is preparing an agreement with that ministry to frame national deployment; the date is that of the interview.
ANIP's director general credits the pilot's results to collaboration with the Ministry of Health, UNICEF and the World Bank-financed project; no domestic budget line is stated.

The pilot closed in February 2026 with a registration rate above 76% and a consolidation phase with new internet-connected terminals opened in the ten facilities, though national generalisation is three to four months late, on ANIP's director general's account.
